subject: Questions about session-specific covariate and hcov

messages.author: 4a881917dcd26316
messages.subject: Questions about session-specific covariate and hcov
parts:
I have just started using secr and have two questions about it. My data is the following;

I have vole capture-mark-recapture data from 1983-2015. Trap sessions were in August from 1983-2015 (Totally 52 sessions). Traps were set in 5 consecutive days in the first week of the month (5 occasions in each session). Voles were checked about their sex, age (juvenile or adult), and weight as individual covariates. Environmental covariates (session-specific covariates) were seed abundance of last year (for density). 

My questions are the following;

1) Zero record session
In 2002, we did set traps in every occasion, but could not capture any only in the year. Although I would like to evaluate that no record with environmental covariates, I do not know how to incorporate that into read.caphist.

2) Double hcov?
As individual covariates, I have age (juvenile and adult) and sex (male and female). Both have missing values, so I wanted to put these two into hcov at the same time. Does anyone have an idea for this issue?  

Sincerely,
Ryo

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Questions about session-specific covariate and hcov
parts:
Hi
1. There is a mechanism for this: include a 'dummy' capture record for the session (with any occasion and trapID), using NONE as the animalID (you can change this with the 'noncapt' argument of read.capthist). At least, that is supposed to work, but I haven't tried it for a long time. This is part of the code that doesn't get much testing, so please
get back to the list if you find 'zero-captures' sessions don't behave as you expect.
2. Unfortunately, I don't have an elegant solution. hcov really only works with a 2-class mixture. You could try age then sex in different models. Or drop captures with missing values (if there aren't a lot) and treat age and sex as individual covariates (use CL = TRUE).
Murray
